newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kazakh govt wants to buy Turanbank shares.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh govt wants to buy Turanbank shares.

text.p: The Kazakh government plans to buy shares in the country's fourth biggest bank, Turanbank, in order to restructure it and find a new investor for it, a senior National Bank official said on Wednesday.
Deputy chairman Grigory Marchenko told Reuters the government would use funds from World Bank credits to buy the shares.
He said Turanbank had accumulated three billion tenge in bad credits, compared with a total credit portfolio of 7.5 billion tenge. The bank's paid-in capital is 800 million tenge.
Marchenko said the owners who had taken over Turanbank when it was privatised in 1995, had not had the staff or funds to manage it properly.

Turanbank's new chairman Bisengali Tadzhiyakov said that some of the bad credits had been granted to companies that now are under foreign management, and repayment had been postponed for 18 months according to the terms of new management.
He said the bank would cut costs and staff.
Marchenko said Kazakhstan needed a system to protect banks against bad debt.
"There are a lot of people who manage to use the same collateral in five banks and get credits in several places simultaneously," he said.

The Kazakh National Bank started on August 1 a 2-1/2 year programme to recapitalise the banking system. Under this plan banks that are unable to meet international norms by 1998 will be stripped of authorisation for key operations.
